test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 25 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: An article is sold at a profit of 20%. If both the cost price and selling price are Rs. 100 less, the profit will be 4% more. Find the cost price.
solution:
Given:

Article sold at a profit of 20%.

If both cost price (CP) and selling price (SP) are reduced by Rs 100, profit increases by 4% (to 24%).

Formula Used:

Initial profit formula: Profit% = (SP - CP) / CP × 100

New situation: New profit% = (SP - 100 - (CP - 100)) / (CP - 100) × 100

Calculation:

From given, initial profit = 20%,

⇒ SP = CP + 0.20 × CP

⇒ SP = 1.20 × CP

With Rs. 100 less in CP and SP, profit = 24%,

⇒ (SP - 100) - (CP - 100) = 0.24 × (CP - 100)

⇒ (1.20CP - 100) - CP + 100 = 0.24 × CP - 24

⇒ 0.20CP = 0.24 × CP - 24 ⇒ 24 = 0.24CP - 0.20CP

⇒ 24 = 0.04CP

⇒ CP = 24 / 0.04

⇒ CP = Rs. 600

Thus, the cost price of the article is Rs. 600.
